messages.body_plain:
I thought this might be the same issue Meng was having.  Thanks for confirming!

I think the problem is conflicting versions for the Mac OS and Xcode.  My (limited) understanding of this is there can be problems induced by updating your Mac OS and leaving your Xcode un-updated.  The dynr team will have to discuss this and see what solution we can find.  In the meantime, this google query and these links may help, but I'm not optimistic about them.

https://www.google.com/search?q=dylib+was+built+for+newer+macOS+version+than+being+linked
https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/20024
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43216273/object-file-was-built-for-newer-osx-version-than-being-linked

-Mike

messages.subject: Re: [External] [dynr] dynr
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jerome,

I am the one with the BigSur laptop (ver. 11.2.3, the same as yours). After the team rummaged through a lot of forums, here are the things I did that eventually resolved the link issue, in steps. I would suggest trying Step 6 first before going down the list. Most of the other steps are just making sure the versions are compatible/there is no hidden old system files. I hope this helps! Let us know if you still encounter the problem!

1. Follow the steps here to remove all previous versions of clang and gfortran, clang4 installer receipt, ~/ .R/Makevars and ~/.Renviron

https://thecoatlessprofessor.com/programming/r/uninstalling-the-r-development-toolchain-on-macos/

2. Remove previous versions of XCode and download + install XCode
3. If you have previously installed Command Line Tools, navigate to /Library/Developer and remove Command Line Tools (*this was the step that allowed me to run Rcpp successfully)
4. Install gfortran that is appropriate for your OS from: https://github.com/fxcoudert/gfortran-for-macOS/releases
5. Re-install R
6. Go to edit /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/etc/Makeconf and remove all compilers’ explicit link to a particular OS; e.g., change ‘'CC=clang -mmacosx-version-min=10.16'’ to just 'CC=clang'
7. Install dynr
8. Test run with demo("LinearSDE")

Best,
Meng
